The 2 `physics` commands of the editor at engine `319075e3f92b`: each with its description, its kind, the MCP toolsets that offer it, its parameters and their JSON Schema (the other groups have files of their own).

## physics.setDetailedStats

Turns box3d's counters (islands; contacts total, awake and recycled) on or off for every step of the running game (play or simulate), where physics.stats {detail: true} reads them once: while on, physics.stats reports them after each step (contacts.detailed is true from the next step on) and the Streaming panel's Physics section shows the share of the awake contacts box3d recycled. box3d counts them together with its memory, about 0.1 ms a step at 70,000 bodies, so they are off by default. Holds for the running scene until play stops; a scene the game switches to starts without them. Fails while editing and when the running scene has no physics. Returns enabled.

Kind: `Session` · Results: `Content` · MCP toolsets: `world` · Answers later (MayDefer): no · Waits for the asset scan: no · Registered at `StrataEditor/src/Editor/EditorWorldCommands.cpp:1076`

## physics.stats

The physics of the running game (play or simulate): bodies in the simulation (total, static, dynamic, kinematic, awake, character controllers; parked: static bodies out of it that collide with nothing until box3d drops them a second later) and the bodies in use, the world's room (maxBodies: as it grew; growthLimit: the most it may hold; maxContactConstraints) and the memory it takes (reservedMB), bodies waiting at the growth limit (waitingForSlot: below it no body waits) and waiting for other reasons (meshes loading, degenerate transforms), the bodies built and destroyed and the milliseconds spent on it in the last frame, the slices a switched-to scene's bodies were built in while it loaded (preparedSlices; 0 when they were built as the scene started), the world's growths past its room (count, the last one's milliseconds and room), what the world needed beyond the room it was created with (demand: the scene's next world reserves it), the last step's milliseconds, the steps run, the steps held while mesh colliders wait for their meshes, and whether the last step was held. What the last step did: step (ms; libraryMs, box3d's own part; strataMs, Strata's, in parts apply, sync, characters, checkedPairs, events, writeBack, pairs and instruments; library: box3d's stages pairs, collide, solve and sensors, which add up to libraryMs, and the parts of solve constraints, transforms, refit, continuous and islands, besides splitIslands; workers: box3d's; totalMs and totalLibraryMs since the running scene's physics world was created: difference two reads of one world, as a scene switch or a restart makes a new world and starts them from 0), sleep (awake, sleeping and moving bodies, islands), contacts (total, awake and recycled: box3d's reuse of resting contacts without new collision work, and recycledShare of the awake ones; tracked: touching entity pairs someone listens to; capacity; peak: the most contacts box3d held; roomGrowths: box3d steps whose new contacts grew its contact storage while playing, counted after the step that follows; lastGrowthStepMs: the library time of the last of them) and settling (maxSpeed of the moving bodies in m/s; settling: those faster than the sleep threshold; restingJitterMm: how far the others still move in a step). box3d's counters (islands; contacts total, awake and recycled) are read every step only while detailed statistics are on (physics.setDetailedStats, the perf lab, a game run with a perf log; contacts.detailed: the last step read them); otherwise detail: true reads them once for this answer (box3d's last step) and changes nothing, and without it they are null. settings: the tuning the world runs with (contactRecycleDistance in meters, sleepThreshold in m/s, contactHertz; effectiveContactHertz: what box3d uses, at most an eighth of its substep rate, 30 at 60 fixed steps per second; contactDampingRatio, contactPushSpeed) and its source (project: the project's Physics.Simulation section, which project.setSettings changes while the game runs, from its next fixed step; defaults); null without a world. interpolation: what is drawn between the last two fixed steps (enabled, stepAlpha: how far between their poses this frame draws; entities; blended: moved by the steps, composed: carried by what moved, exact: drawn where it is). {running: false} while editing; simulating is false while a running scene has no physics components.
